problem_text:
A logistics manager is assembling a fleet of cargo drones for a critical three-day humanitarian airlift mission. They must select a combination of supply containers to maximize total priority score while staying within the maximum payload limit of the lead transport aircraft.

The available containers are:
* Container A: weight 15 tons, priority 158 units
* Container B: weight 38 tons, priority 171 units
* Container C: weight 2 tons, priority 194 units
* Container D: weight 3 tons, priority 228 units
* Container E: weight 47 tons, priority 22 units
* Container F: weight 37 tons, priority 290 units
* Container G: weight 2 tons, priority 34 units
* Container H: weight 4 tons, priority 218 units
* Container I: weight 40 tons, priority 163 units
* Container J: weight 29 tons, priority 179 units
* Container K: weight 42 tons, priority 23 units
* Container L: weight 36 tons, priority 205 units
* Container M: weight 7 tons, priority 225 units
* Container N: weight 18 tons, priority 32 units
* Container O: weight 22 tons, priority 32 units
* Container P: weight 4 tons, priority 188 units
* Container Q: weight 42 tons, priority 70 units
* Container R: weight 40 tons, priority 17 units
* Container S: weight 41 tons, priority 279 units
* Container T: weight 41 tons, priority 60 units
* Container U: weight 37 tons, priority 286 units
* Container V: weight 3 tons, priority 118 units
* Container W: weight 38 tons, priority 220 units
* Container X: weight 18 tons, priority 61 units

Furthermore, due to a compatibility constraint, exactly one of Container A or Container B must be included in the shipment.

If Container C is selected, it necessitates the inclusion of a special cooling unit that reduces the effective aircraft payload capacity by 10 tons.
The lead aircraft has a maximum payload capacity of 424 tons. The manager must determine the optimal set of containers to load.
